takeaway: Basal cell carcinoma: the commonest skin cancer, a slowly enlarging pearly white lesion with telangiectasia, usually on the head and neck, destroying tissue locally.

question.text: An 80-year-old retired builder has a chronic, slowly enlarging skin lesion on his left cheek. It is pearly white with telangiectasia. What is the diagnosis?
question.say: An eighty-year-old retired builder has a chronic and slowly enlarging skin lesion on his left cheek. It is pearly white, with an associated telangiectasia. What is the diagnosis?

answer.say: The answer is basal cell carcinoma.

lines.text: A retired builder with a chronic, slowly enlarging lesion on his left cheek.
lines.say: This eighty-year-old retired builder has a chronic, slowly enlarging skin lesion on his left cheek.
(laugh) The lesion is pearly white, like a little pearl on his cheek.

lines.text: Tiny red vessels run across it: telangiectasia.
lines.say: Tiny red vessels run across it. That is telangiectasia.

lines.text: The little excavator shows local destruction of the tissue around it.
lines.say: The little excavator shows local destruction. It invades and destroys the surrounding tissues.

lines.text: It is the most common skin cancer, mostly on the head and neck: 80 per cent.
lines.say: It is the most common type of skin cancer, and most lesions are on the head and neck, about eighty per cent.

lines.text: Remember: a pearly white lesion with telangiectasia is basal cell carcinoma.
lines.say: Remember: a pearly white lesion with telangiectasia is a basal cell carcinoma.
